text.p: Brazilian police arrested Antonio Graca Mota, one of the country's most notorious drug traffickers, who was on the run since he escaped from jail in 1993, a police spokesman said on Tuesday.
Graca Mota, who also known as "Cocaine King", is accused of ties to Colombia's Cali Cartel and running the Brazilian leg of the drug route between Colombia and Europe.

Police said that in 1993 Graca Mota bribed his way out of Sao Paulo's Carandiru jail, where he was serving a 10 year sentence for drug trafficking, and that he has been living mostly outside the country ever since.
Police said Graca Mota was captured on Monday by federal agents when he stopped to buy cigarettes at a gas station on his way to the Sao Paulo airport.
They said Graca Mota had returned to Brazil after a four-year absence to visit his children who live in the interior of the state of Sao Paulo.

In an interview at the Sao Paulo Federal Police station, Graca Mota denied any links to the drug business or to the Cali Cartel. "This is all a big invention of the press and of the police," he told reporters.
